editorial.headline: Sharia Venture Capital, With Bali’s Risk Line in View
editorial.standfirst: A fully Sharia-based venture-capital activity, open nationally to foreign investment at every listed scale and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Sharia venture capital is not simply capital with a faith-based label. This activity covers venture-capital operations, venture-fund management and related business carried out wholly under Sharia principles. Its practical field includes equity participation and time-bound financing for the development of partner businesses at the early start-up or business-development stage, as well as profit-sharing finance, services and other approved activities. The underlying idea is developmental capital for an operating partner business, structured within Sharia principles rather than outside them.

The investment toolkit is defined with useful precision. It can include equity participation, the purchase of sukuk or convertible Sharia bonds, and the purchase of sukuk or Sharia bonds issued by a partner business at an early start-up or development stage. Profit-sharing financing and services also sit within the activity. It is a regulated business form: the enterprise undertaking these Sharia venture-capital, fund-management and related activities does so with the approval of the Financial Services Authority, and its other activities likewise require that authority’s approval.

The registration picture is broad at the national level. The activity is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, and it is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That breadth should not obscure the character of the activity itself: this is a business built around Sharia-compliant investment, finance and fund management, rather than a generic commercial-services registration.

Bali does not turn that national opening into a prohibition. The province’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium blocks activities assessed at Low and Medium-Low risk. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. Bali’s status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, meaning the relevant local picture is not a PMA ban but a higher-risk classification at that scale. For a foreign investor considering Bali, the honest conclusion is straightforward: this activity remains registrable for PMA there, while its large-scale risk position must be read as part of the registration context.
